commitResults.messageTitle: Support MVP punctuation in player names
commitResults.messageBody:
The inherited name validation rejects slash-containing names, so the
MVP example find s/o cannot match a stored player.

Accept the punctuation allowed by the MVP name specification while
retaining validation of blank names and disallowed characters. Cover
name validation and storage conversion so these records remain usable
across sessions.

Refs #49

commitResults.messageTitle: Align player searches with the F3 specification
commitResults.messageBody:
The inherited find command reports person(s) and attempts to save the
team after every search, which can hide search results behind unrelated
storage errors.

Use the exact MVP usage and singular/plural feedback, and return search
results without writing player data. Retain whole-word, case-insensitive
OR matching and add regression coverage for literal slash keywords,
missing keywords, repeated searches, and filtered deletion.

Refs #49

commitResults.messageTitle: Document F3 searches and manual regression checks
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide describes inherited contact searches without the MVP
feedback or search-error examples, and the manual test plan has no
find scenarios.

Document the player-name matching rules, exact messages, and filtered
indices. Add repeatable JavaFX checks using disposable data, including
unavailable storage and loading a saved slash-containing name.

Refs #49

trialists by position, role, or their own categories.

Add repeatable labels to add/edit, display them on player cards, and
persist them without breaking older data files. Preserve tags when
omitted during edits and support explicit replacement or clearing.

Document the behavior and model UML, and test validation, immutable
collections, persistence, and JavaFX command-box interactions.

commitResults.messageBody:

cannot overwrite saved data or fail because saving is unavailable.

Document the command, help, UML relationships, and regression cases.
Test matching, invalid input, filtered indices, saving, and JavaFX
flows.

Refs #85

commitResults.messageBody:

"persons" in an "address book", which does not match CouchCoach,
where coaches manage players in a team.

Let's align the delete command's usage, success and invalid-index
messages, and its UG section, with the F4 spec. The invalid-index
message is shared with edit, so edit now also reports an invalid
"player" index.

Also test that decimal indices such as 2.5 are rejected, which the
spec requires but no existing test checked.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match F7 save-failure message and stop exit saving
commitResults.messageBody:
A failed save shows AB3's message, which does not tell the coach what
to do and exposes the data file's full path. exit also saves, so
exiting right after starting with an unreadable data file overwrites
that file with an empty team, which the F7 spec rules out.

Let's show the spec's save-failure message and log the technical
cause instead, and treat exit like list, find and help, which never
write the data file.

Fixes #57
Fixes #59

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn on startup when the data file is unreadable
commitResults.messageBody:
When the data file cannot be read, CouchCoach starts with an empty
team but only reports the problem in the terminal log, so the coach
sees an empty list with no explanation.

Let's show the F7 spec's warning in the result box when the window
opens, so the coach knows the data will be replaced on the next
change and can repair or back up the file first.

Fixes #58

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the user guide for CouchCoach v1.3
commitResults.messageBody:
Much of the user guide still describes AB3: the intro, quick start
and download link, the t/TAG examples, the old help window and its
known issue, the edit and clear sections, and the saving and data
file sections.

Let's describe CouchCoach throughout, document help as the in-app
summary, explain which commands save and what happens when saving
or loading fails, add exit to the command summary, and remove the
unused help window screenshot.

Fixes #61

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that the UI shows the startup warning
commitResults.messageBody:
No test starts the UI, so nothing checks that a startup message from
MainApp reaches the result box when the window opens.

message and check what the result box shows.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test MainApp startup and shutdown
commitResults.messageBody:
MainApp has no tests, as it always uses the real data and preference
files in the working directory. So nothing checks that an unreadable
data file leads to the startup warning, and the startup lines added
for that warning are reported as untested.

Let's let tests point MainApp at files in a temporary folder, and
test starting with no data file, with an unreadable one, and saving
preferences on stop. Also describe the app as CouchCoach V1.3 in its
startup and shutdown log messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain how to recover from a failed save in the UG
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG tells the coach to fix the problem after a failed save, but
fixing it does not save the change and exit does not save either,
while the exit section promises that nothing is lost.

Let's list the steps to get the change saved: fix the problem, then
make another change, since every save writes the whole team. Also
qualify the exit section, as exit does not save.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add selection status to players
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches running trials need to record whether each player is kept or
cut, but a player only holds a name and phone number.

Let's give every player a selection status of pending, kept or cut.
New players start as pending. The status is saved with the player,
and data files from v1.3, which have no status, load as pending.

Editing a player keeps their status, as edit is not meant to undo a
selection decision.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add keep, cut and pending commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches have no way to set a player's selection status, and the list
does not show it.

Let's add the keep, cut and pending commands, which set the status of
the player at the given index in the displayed list. They share one
SetStatusCommand, as they differ only in the status they set. The
displayed list is not reset, so a coach can keep working through the
results of a find.

Each player card shows the status as a badge. The badge always shows
the status as text, so it does not rely on colour alone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document keep, cut and pending in the user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide does not mention the new selection commands, and its
list of commands that save data is out of date.

Let's add a section for keep, cut and pending, add them to the
command summary, and list them among the commands that save.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add squad command to view kept players
commitResults.messageBody:
After marking players as kept, coaches cannot see their squad on its
own, as the list mixes kept, cut and pending players.

Let's add a squad command that shows only the kept players and says
how many there are. It reuses the filtered list, like find, so list
shows everyone again. It does not change player data, so it does not
save.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document squad in the user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Let's add a section for the squad command, add it to the command
summary, and list it among the commands that take no parameters and
do not save.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add cut sequence diagram to the developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide does not explain how the keep, cut and pending
commands work.

Let's add a selection status section under Implementation, with a
sequence diagram showing how cut 1 runs through Logic, Model and
Storage, and the design choices behind the shared SetStatusCommand.

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement add command for players
commitResults.messageBody:
Reduce the player record to a name and phone number, as required by
MVP feature F1, and remove the now unused email, address and tag
fields and classes.

Names are trimmed with repeated internal spaces collapsed, may contain
letters, digits, spaces and - ' / . and are limited to 100 characters.
Phones allow an optional leading '+' and 3 to 15 digits, with spaces
and hyphens stripped before storing.

Two players are duplicates if their names match ignoring case and
repeated spaces; the phone number is not compared. A repeated prefix
in add now takes its last value instead of being rejected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update UG and DG for the add command
Match name validation regex with the find PR

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract name and phone normalization into model
commitResults.messageBody:
ParserUtil#parseName and Name#isSameName each had their own copy of
the regex that trims a name and collapses repeated spaces, so the two
could drift apart.

Let's move the logic into Name#normalize and Phone#normalize, give
the phone separator regex a name, and use American spelling to match
the rest of the codebase.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JerseyNumber to represent a player's jersey number
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches identify players by their jersey numbers in trial notes and
videos, but there is no way to represent one yet.

Add a JerseyNumber class that accepts whole numbers from 0 to 99. A
leading zero is dropped so that "07" and "7" are the same number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Store an optional jersey number for each player
commitResults.messageBody:
Each player should be able to carry a jersey number, but Person and
its saved form only hold a name and a phone number.

Let's
* add an optional jersey number to Person, kept as a constructor
  without it for players who have none
* save the jersey number with the player, leaving the field out when
  the player has none

Data files saved by v1.3 have no jersey number field, so they still
load, with no player having a jersey number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let add take an optional jersey number
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches want to record a player's jersey number when they add the
player, but add only takes a name and a phone number.

Let's
* add a j/ prefix that add accepts as an optional jersey number
* show the jersey number in the player details of result messages

As with the other add fields, the last j/ value is used if the prefix
is repeated.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let edit change or remove a player's jersey number
commitResults.messageBody:
Coaches need to fix a jersey number after adding a player, or remove
it when the player gives the number up, but edit cannot change it.

Let's
* let edit take j/JERSEY to change the jersey number
* treat an empty j/ as removing the jersey number

EditPersonDescriptor tracks whether the jersey number was edited,
because a null jersey number alone cannot tell "leave it unchanged"
apart from "remove it".

commitResults.messageTitle: Show jersey numbers on player cards and in the help panel
commitResults.messageBody:
Jersey numbers can be added and edited, but coaches cannot see them
in the player list, and the help panel does not say how to set them.

Let's
* show "Jersey #N" on the card of each player that has a jersey number,
  hiding the line for players without one
* add [j/JERSEY] to add in the help panel, together with an edit entry
  that explains how to change or remove a jersey number
* give most sample players a jersey number, so that new users see the
  field in use

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Person#hasSameJerseyNumber to compare jersey numbers
commitResults.messageBody:
Commands need to find other players who wear the same jersey number,
but comparing two optional jersey numbers is easy to get wrong when
one or both players have none.

Add Person#hasSameJerseyNumber, which is true only when both players
have a jersey number and it is the same number.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn the coach when two players share a jersey number
commitResults.messageBody:
Two players with the same jersey number usually means a typo, but add
and edit accept it silently, so the mistake goes unnoticed.

Let's
* let add and edit still make the change, but append a warning that
  names the other players with the same jersey number
* only warn on edit when the edit sets the jersey number, so editing
  other details of such a player does not repeat the warning

The change is not rejected because teams can reuse a number, e.g.
for players in different squads.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document jersey numbers in the user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide does not mention the j/ prefix, so coaches cannot
learn how to record, change or remove a jersey number.

Let's
* add [j/JERSEY] to the add and edit formats, with its rules and
  examples
* explain that an empty j/ removes the jersey number
* describe the warning shown when players share a jersey number
* update the command summary

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the saved jersey number in the storage class diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG does not show what JsonAdaptedPerson saves, and still says each
Person holds only a name and a phone number.

Let's
* show the fields of JsonAdaptedPerson in StorageClassDiagram, with a
  note that the jersey number is left out when a player has none
* explain in the Storage section how optional fields are saved, so
  that older data files still load
* mention the optional jersey number in the Model section

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a redrawn image for the storage class diagram
commitResults.messageBody:
The storage class diagram should show what JsonAdaptedPerson saves,
including the optional jersey number, in a form that is easy to read
in the DG.

Let's
* add StorageClassDiagram.png, a redrawn class diagram that shows the
  key operations, the multiplicities and the optional jerseyNumber
  field of JsonAdaptedPerson
* show that image in the Storage section in place of the PlantUML
  diagram

StorageClassDiagram.puml is kept and updated as the text source that
teammates can edit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge upstream master and preserve jersey numbers
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags, ratings, selection status, remarks and injury status were added
to Person while jersey numbers were in review, so Person, its saved
form, the add and edit parsers, the player card and the help panel all
conflicted.

Let's
* add the jersey number to the full Person constructor and to every
  with* copy method, plus a new Person#withJerseyNumber
* keep the jersey number when RateCommand rebuilds a rated player,
  which would otherwise drop it
* save the jersey number with the other optional fields, leaving only
  that field out when it is absent, so other fields save as before
* show j/ alongside t/ in the add and edit help entries

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that jersey numbers survive a JSON round trip
commitResults.messageBody:
JsonAdaptedPersonTest only converts between Person and the adapter,
so it does not check the JSON that is actually written to disk.

Add a test that serializes players with JsonUtil and reads them back,
checking that j/07 is written as 7 and that a player without a jersey
number is written without the jerseyNumber field.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch '82-jersey-number' into 83-duplicate-jersey-warning
Cover more cases of the shared jersey number warning
commitResults.messageBody:
The warning tests do not check numbers written differently, a jersey
number of 0, players hidden by a filter, or removing a shared number.

Let's
* check that 07 and 7 count as the same number
* check that 0 is only shared with another 0, not with no number
* check that a teammate hidden by find is still named in the warning
* check that removing a shared number with an empty j/ gives no warning

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge upstream master and keep the jersey number docs
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags, filtering, selection status, ratings, remarks and injury status
changed the add and edit sections, the command summary and the Model
section while the jersey number docs were in review.

Let's
* list j/ alongside t/ in the add and edit formats and summary
* keep the shared jersey number and repeated-prefix rules in add
* add the optional JerseyNumber to the Model section's field list and
  identity rules, and note that the model diagrams do not show it yet

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain when edit keeps a jersey number or repeats the warning
commitResults.messageBody:
The edit section says how to remove a jersey number, but not that
leaving out j/ keeps it, that only edit accepts an empty j/, or that
the shared number warning only appears when the edit includes j/.

Spell out all three cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the storage diagram source and clarify optional fields
commitResults.messageBody:
The storage diagram PNG has no editable source in the repo, and the

commitResults.messageTitle: Guide unknown commands to help
commitResults.messageBody:
The parser gives no command-discovery hint, and the command box ignores
blank input.

Prompt coaches to type help for unknown or blank commands, and route empty
input through the parser so the result box shows the same useful feedback.
Cover whitespace-only input, misspellings, and command-word case in parser
regression tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show CouchCoach help in the main window
commitResults.messageBody:
Help opens an AddressBook popup containing only a user-guide URL and
attempts to save unchanged player data.

Replace the popup with a scrollable command summary in the player-list
area. Keep the Help menu and F1 shortcut, and restore the player panel
after successful commands without changing the filter when help is shown.

Skip storage writes for help so coaches can view the summary even when
the data file cannot be written. Cover unchanged player data and filtered
lists, empty teams, and invalid input with logic regression tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename the main window to CouchCoach
Enable JavaFX tests in CI
commitResults.messageBody:
The test suite does not initialize JavaFX, and the Linux runner has no
display for tests that construct UI controls.

Add a shared utility that runs test actions on the JavaFX Application
Thread, waits for failures to propagate, and keeps the runtime available
between tests. Run the Linux Gradle checks under a virtual display so the
same UI tests participate in the normal coverage build on every platform.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the inline help panel
commitResults.messageBody:
The help panel constructor has no coverage in the JUnit suite.

Verify that its actual FXML control contains the MVP command formats,
examples, and usage guidance. Check that the summary is read-only, wraps
within the available width, and starts at the beginning of the text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test help transitions through the main window
commitResults.messageBody:
The UI paths that show help and restore the player panel are not covered
by the normal coverage build.

Exercise the command box, Help menu, and F1 event handlers using real
JavaFX controls. Verify repeated help requests, player-command transitions,
unknown and blank command feedback, unchanged filters and player data,
and the CouchCoach window title.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use the regular app font in help
commitResults.messageBody:
The help summary uses a monospace font and shows the text area's rounded
corner marks against the dark panel.

Match the regular font used by the result box and remove rounded
background layers from the help control. Replace space-padded columns
with simple command lines so the summary remains readable with a
proportional font, including at the minimum window width.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align help columns with the MVP document
commitResults.messageBody:
The regular-font summary puts command descriptions inline, losing the
document's column alignment and indentation of examples.

Display command syntax in a fixed left column and descriptions and
examples in a wrapping right column. Keep the regular font and flat panel
styling, and place the automatic-saving note below the command grid.

Define the summary in the FXML layout and adapt the existing UI tests to
the scrollable label content.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test help column alignment at both window widths
commitResults.messageBody:
The command and description columns must remain aligned in a regular
font, including when the window is reduced to its minimum width.

Check the rendered positions of all six command rows at normal and
minimum widths. Verify that descriptions align with each other and their
commands, wrap within the window, and do not overlap the syntax column.

commitResults.messageTitle: Hint how to return from help to the player list
commitResults.messageBody:
Help hides the player list while index-based commands still act on the
previously displayed players.

Add a visible prompt to type list below the help heading so coaches know
how to see their players again. Check the hint in the existing help
content test.
